/-- **The order `R_I`** of a nonarchimedean packet: the `ℤ_p`-span of the elementary tensors
of integral tuples, i.e. the image of `⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝓞_{c j}`. -/
noncomputable def orderSubmodule : Submodule ℤ_[p] (Tensor K (.finite p) c) :=
  Submodule.span ℤ_[p] (integralSet p c)
assumptions: binders: {K : Type u} [Field K] [NumberField K] {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (p : Nat.Primes) (c : ι → Place K) [Integral.lean:43, :175]; no ramification/finiteness hypothesis; depends on def integralSet/tprodIntegral (Integral.lean:178-185) and on the ℤ_p-algebra structure instAlgebraPadicIntTensor (Integral.lean:189-193, restriction of scalars along ℤ_p → ℚ_p). Result: Submodule ℤ_[p] (Tensor K (.finite p) c), the ℤ_p-span of integralSet.
source_claim_supported: SOURCE_FACT: the 'tensor order' is defined as the ℤ_p-span of the image of integral elementary tensors; the docstring's identification with the image of ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝓞_{c j} is prose only — no isomorphism with an abstract tensor-product ring is stated in Lean ⇒ faithfulness of the name UNRESOLVED; do not read this as an integral closure (that is S2).

/-- **The integral structure `(R_I)^∼`** of a nonarchimedean packet: the integral closure of
`ℤ_p` in the packet, i.e. its ring of integers (`LocalTheory.integral` at a prime; IUT IV,
Proposition 1.2). -/
noncomputable def integral : Set (Tensor K (.finite p) c) :=
  integralClosure ℤ_[p] (Tensor K (.finite p) c)
assumptions: binders: {K : Type u} [Field K] [NumberField K] {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (p : Nat.Primes) (c : ι → Place K) [MaximalOrder.lean:57, :96]; no extra hypothesis; definition is Mathlib integralClosure ℤ_[p] (Tensor K (.finite p) c), needing only the ℤ_p-algebra structure (Integral.lean:189-193). Result is a Set; the only additive packaging is integralAddSubgroup (MaximalOrder.lean:323-324).
source_claim_supported: SOURCE_FACT: the maximal order (R_I)^∼ is *defined* as the integral closure of ℤ_p in the packet, so it is not the tensor order; only order_subset_integral (MaximalOrder.lean:191) is proved, strictness/equality is not. The identification with IUT IV Prop. 1.2 appears in the docstring only (prose), so text faithfulness is UNRESOLVED.

/-- **The residue-field decomposition** of the packet (a reduced Artinian ring). -/
noncomputable def residueEquiv :
    Tensor K (.finite p) c ≃ₐ[Tensor K (.finite p) c] ∀ m, ResidueField p c m :=
  IsArtinianRing.equivPi _
assumptions: binders: {K : Type u} [Field K] [NumberField K] {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (p : Nat.Primes) (c : ι → Place K) [ResidueField.lean:44-45]; needs IsArtinianRing and IsReduced instances on the packet (MaximalOrder.lean:235 isArtinianRing_tensor, :104 isReduced_tensor) so that Mathlib's IsArtinianRing.equivPi applies; base ring is the packet itself (≃ₐ[Tensor K (.finite p) c]).
source_claim_supported: SOURCE_FACT: a *ring-level* algebra equivalence onto the finite product of residue fields (indices = MaximalSpectrum), not merely a ℚ_p-linear iso, and not a decomposition into the local-field factors ∏_j K_{c j}; a factor-wise product decomposition has no signature in this repo ⇒ 'ambient tensor algebra → product of local fields' UNRESOLVED.

/-- **`(R_I)^∼` is the product of the closed unit balls of the residue fields.** -/
theorem mem_integral_iff_forall_resNorm_le_one {x : Tensor K (.finite p) c} :
    x ∈ integral p c ↔ ∀ m, resNorm p c m (proj p c m x) ≤ 1 := by
  rw [mem_integral_iff_forall_isIntegral]
  exact forall_congr' fun m => isIntegral_iff_resNorm_le_one _
assumptions: binders as in S3 plus (m : MaximalSpectrum (Tensor K (.finite p) c)) [ResidueField.lean:53]; resNorm := spectralNorm ℚ_[p] (ResidueField p c m) (ResidueField.lean:89-90), proj := Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ (ResidueField.lean:66-67); uses mem_integral_iff_forall_isIntegral (:172-173) and isIntegral_iff_resNorm_le_one (:125-126); no extra hypothesis.
source_claim_supported: SOURCE_FACT: the order/decomposition correspondence is given pointwise as a norm criterion (x ∈ (R_I)^∼ ↔ ∀ 𝔪, ‖x mod 𝔪‖ ≤ 1); the docstring calls this 'the product of the closed unit balls', but no statement identifies (R_I)^∼ with the image of a product subring under residueEquiv ⇒ ring-level correspondence UNRESOLVED.
